_comment: rules for scan_sorter.py - all patterns are case-insensitive Python regexes.
A page scores each source/type by number of matches; a hit in the top ~500
chars of the page also earns a +2 'heading' bonus. First match wins exact
score ties, so put more specific rules earlier.
Pages that match nothing go to default_source/default_type.
strong_start_patterns: line-anchored signals that a page likely BEGINS a new
document (used by boundary detection, only counted near the top of the page).
continuation_markers: signals a page is a CONTINUATION (not a new document).
How the final .pdf of each sorted document is named.
'instructions' are fed to the LLM verbatim as naming rules - edit freely.
tax_types / les_types / les_text_indicators drive the deterministic (no-LLM)
fallback: type names are matched case-insensitively, indicators are case-insensitive regexes searched in the document text.
instructions: 1) Default (most documents): <source>_<type>_<yyyy-mm-dd>. Lowercase the source and type, spaces become hyphens. Example: acme-invoice_2025-10-30.pdf
2) If the type name already contains the source word (e.g. bank + bank_statement), write it only once. Example: bank-statement_2025-10-01.pdf

3) Tax documents (1099 series, W-2, 1040, T4 and any other tax form): <tax_year>_<type>_<source>_<yyyy-mm-dd>. The date is one printed on the form; if no date is printed use <tax_year>-12-31, the end of the tax year. Example: 2025_1099-nec_irs_2025-12-31.pdf
4) LES documents: use only <les>_<yyyy-mm> (the statement's year and month, no day). Example: les_2026-05.pdf
5) Only use dates that actually appear in the document; never invent a date. For statements or bills covering a period, prefer the period end date or the issue/remit date.
6) If the document has no usable date at all, omit the date part entirely (keep source and type).
7) Filename: lowercase, only a-z 0-9 plus _ and -; must end in .pdf; no path, no spaces. Answer with exactly one filename.
